description: Reference-machine performance baseline for the hook hot path (R6-02). Recorded by `node scripts/perf-baseline.js --slo --json` plus `--surface=dual-cold --runs=15`. Schema v2 separates conservative aggregate process cost (sum of per-hook p95 values) from concurrent event wall latency (p95 until all matching hook processes exit). Thresholds live in qa/perf/slo.json and operator policy in spec/OPERATOR.md §O9.
sloVerdict: PASS (2 rounds x 15 runs/hook, aggregate and concurrent-wall rounds stable on single and dual-warm)
notes: The former absolute dual-warm overhead mixed sequential p95 sums with wall latency. On this 17-hook capture the same PreToolUse workload is 495.9 -> 1143.5 ms aggregate but only 109.3 -> 133.0 ms concurrent wall.
dual-cold clears the isolated arbitration cache before every sample. Both physical copies therefore run full work; its PreToolUse aggregate is 1028.0 ms and concurrent wall is 126.9 ms.

Worst graded per-hook p95 fraction of timeout is 5.9% (dual-warm standalone memory-read-check: 175.7 / 3000 ms), below the 50% headroom limit. The new pre-mutation and post-tool journal handlers measured 123.5 / 108.7 ms respectively on that surface.
The perf harness does not invoke Codex; the Codex version labels the local runtime environment only. Full runtime conformance is recorded separately.
